office_does: The sheriff runs county law enforcement, the county jail, civil process and emergency operations, patrolling the unincorporated county, for a four-year term.
race_blurb: Sheriff Derek Sanders, an independent elected in 2022, won 71% in the primary against Kevin Burton-Crow, a Democrat, special victims detective and president of the deputies' union. Sanders runs on staffing growth and his first-term record; Burton-Crow runs on outside accreditation, published policies and outcome-based accountability.

candidates.summary: One-term sheriff (Prefers Independent Party) with 12 years in law enforcement, running on staffing growth, training and de-escalation and a proposed mental-health wing at the jail.
highlights: Campaign says patrol deputies rose from 33 to 55 and detectives from 8 to 18 during his term [S3]
Proposes a secured jail mental-health wing run by mental health professionals [S4]
Defended vehicle pursuits in 2025, saying pursuits enabled a gang-member arrest [S7]
Asked the Salary Commission to freeze his own salary in 2025 and 2026 [S6]
Won the August primary with 70.69% of the vote [S5]

safety.basis: Emphasizes deputy staffing, recruitment and vehicle pursuits, paired with de-escalation training and a professionally run mental-health wing at the jail.

spending.basis: Pledges investment in employees, facilities and equipment while promising stewardship of taxpayer dollars and freezing his own salary.

experience.basis: Incumbent sheriff since 2023 with 12 years in law enforcement, running on his first-term record.

reform.basis: Runs on continuing the office's current direction, with accountability measures such as supervisor review of body-camera footage after use of force.

candidates.summary: Sheriff's Office special victims detective, retired Army sergeant first class and president of the deputies' union (Prefers Democratic Party), running for the first time on accreditation, transparency and prevention-focused policing.
highlights: Would seek outside accreditation through the state sheriffs and police chiefs association and publish office policies [S1][S4]
Says deputies should be judged on community impact "not just by how many stops or arrests they make" [S4]
Pledges victim-centered and harm-reduction training and clear annual budget disclosures [S1]
Endorsed by the Thurston County Democrats, the sheriff's captains' association and the Central Labor Council [S5]

safety.basis: Pamphlet and platform measure success by prevention, recovery and community outcomes, with harm-reduction training and an early-intervention abatement team.

spending.basis: Ties spending to measurable outcomes, annual program reports and budget disclosures, and argues accreditation reduces liability costs.

experience.basis: First-time candidate who has not held elected office or command rank, though he has 11 years in the office and a 20-year Army career.

reform.basis: Platform centers outside accreditation, a full policy review, published policies and changes to the field training model.
